paras.t:

sections.name: Header – Find it, fix it, document it properly
sections.title: Find it, fix it, document it properly

cards.title: Find it
cards.text: A crash-focused exam: how the crash happened, which direction, whether you were braced, where you felt it first. Digital X-rays on site. Because disc injuries are more likely after a crash, Dr. Morgan refers most car accident patients for an MRI.

cards.title: Fix it
cards.text: Adjustments, and spinal decompression where imaging supports it. Crash injuries are usually acute, so care starts frequent to stabilize things. Plans typically run 24 to 48 visits.

cards.title: Document it
cards.text: Every visit is recorded properly. If your case involves an insurer or an attorney, the paperwork holds up, and we coordinate records with their office.

sections.name: Conditions Section
sections.title: How personal injury care gets paid for

paras.t: PIP (Personal Injury Protection)
Your own auto coverage. In Texas, policies include at least $2,500 unless you rejected it in writing, and it pays no matter who caused the crash.
The at-fault driver's insurance
Their liability coverage pays for your treatment, usually when the case settles.
In most cases, you pay nothing at the time of service. We don't bill health insurance for car accidents. If none of these apply, we'll tell you up front what care would cost.
Personal injury forms →

cards.title: Letter of protection
cards.text: If you have an attorney, they send us a letter of protection. You're treated now, and the bill is paid from your settlement.

faqs.q: Do I need an attorney to be seen?
faqs.a: No. You can be seen without one. If you already have an attorney, we'll work with their office on records and billing.
In most cases, no. PIP, a letter of protection, or a third-party claim usually covers it. We'll confirm which applies before treatment starts.
It depends on the injury. Plans typically run 24 to 48 visits, with more frequent visits at the start.
Often, yes. Disc injuries are more likely after a crash, so Dr. Morgan refers most car accident patients for one.
